s: a hidden, light-filled courtyard café behind an Old Town tenement facade
w: A specialty coffee shop at the end of Piwna Street whose real draw is invisible from the street -- a 90-square-metre covered courtyard behind the tenement, pale stone and columns catching the light in a way that feels almost Mediterranean. Breakfast, cake and wine alongside the coffee, in a calm space a few steps but a world away from Castle Square's crowds.
_facts: Located at ul. Piwna 40/42, 00-288 Warszawa, Stare Miasto
Specialty coffee shop built around a hidden covered courtyard (patio) not visible from the street
Courtyard space is roughly 90 m², used for events as well as regular service
A short walk from Castle Square, off the main Old Town tourist route

s: arguably the most hidden café in the Old Town, up a stair and mostly locals
w: Reached up a stair through a small anteroom on Nowomiejska Street, this tiny first-floor room looks down over the street below and runs on homemade cakes and coffee made with evident care by the owner. Easy to walk straight past -- which is exactly why it stays a locals' spot rather than a stop on the Old Town circuit.
_facts: Located at ul. Nowomiejska 10 (1st floor), 00-271 Warszawa, Stare Miasto
Small first-floor café reached via a stair from a street-level anteroom
Known for homemade cakes and owner-made coffee
Considered one of the more hidden, locals-only cafés in the Old Town

s: a café and antiquarian bookshop combined on Praga's market street
w: Part café, part secondhand bookshop, on Targowa near the old Różyca market -- old volumes and prints stacked around mismatched furniture, coffee and cake served at a pace that assumes you're staying a while. A quieter, browsier note in Praga's otherwise loud, market-driven street life.
_facts: Located at ul. Targowa 18, lok. 33, 03-731 Warszawa, Praga-Północ (entrance from ul. Mackiewicza)
Combines a café with an antiquarian/secondhand bookshop (antykwariat)
Situated near Targowa street and the historic Różyca market area of Praga
